title: Quick-fix worktrees: smoke test, then merge in seconds

message.text: Sent to the Servex mastermind, with your words verbatim. (1) The rule: nothing merges into michael/dev until a smoke test passes (pages load, no console errors); a full UI test comes after. (2) One smoke script. (3) Three warm quick-fix worktrees, each with its own server and a standing fixer agent: a quick fix goes to a free one, then fix, smoke test, merge within seconds. The free slots will show on Live.

The brief is ready: /framework/ai/2026-09-25/quickfix-worktrees/ (requirements.md, with task.jsonl opened). It asks for five things: the smoke-before-merge rule, Server/smoke.mjs, three warm quickfix slots with a fixer each, routing through quick_fix(), and the slots on Live. Servex won't let me spawn a task mastermind, so the owner's tab starts it: a Sonnet task-mastermind at medium effort, named quickfix-worktrees.

Changed, with no fixer agents and no manager. A pool starts with one ready worktree. Any agent calls take_worktree() and gets back the id, path and URL, then writes, smoke-tests and merges. Taking one makes Servex prepare the next, return_worktree(id) hands an unused one back, and idle extras get pruned. A skill section teaches every minion and mastermind how to use it.

The brief is corrected to a pool with no manager: one ready worktree, which any agent grabs with take_worktree(). Servex prepares the next, return_worktree() hands one back, and idle extras are pruned (at most 3, idle 6 hours). The minion and sub-mastermind skills get a five-line "take, write, smoke-test, merge, return" section, and it's still waiting for the owner's tab to dispatch.

Ready to dispatch, but Servex refuses to let mastermind-servex-2 start a task mastermind. The owner's tab starts it: an Opus task-mastermind named quickfix-worktrees, with the exact call at /framework/ai/2026-09-25/servex-mastermind/ (dispatch.md).

Taken: I own the quick-fix worktrees task and will build it in one worktree of its own. First the smoke script and the rule, then the pool with take_worktree/return_worktree, proven on a private Servex before the live one restarts.

Three minions are building in one worktree: the smoke test plus a one-at-a-time merge script, the pool with take_worktree and return_worktree, and the pool on the Live card. Briefs are in /framework/ai/2026-09-25/quickfix-worktrees/ (smoke, pool, live).

The smoke test works both ways: a clean worktree passes, and a page importing a missing file fails with that file named. The Live card now has a Worktrees list (ready, taken by whom, for how long); the pool behind it is still being built.

The pool works on a private Servex: a take answers in 58 ms and the next worktree is ready 6 s later, with 14 of 14 checks passing. My first merge attempt was refused by the new smoke test itself, because of a shell path quirk, which is now being fixed before the merge.

Incident, now recovered: my merge attempt at 19:04 made git reset 85 files you had uncommitted in the main tree (CLAUDE.md, skills, Servex). All 85 were restored two minutes later from the copy git kept, and nothing was lost. merge.mjs is being changed so git merge never runs over uncommitted edits again.

merge.mjs now merges each file three ways into the working tree, and writes nothing if any file conflicts; it passes 41 of 41 checks on a scratch repo. A dry run on the real tree found one true conflict with uncommitted Live-card work, and the pool rows are being redone on top of that work before landing.

Everything is now in the main tree, uncommitted beside your other work, with the Live page smoke-tested before its reload went out. Restarting Servex now, which turns on take_worktree and return_worktree.

Landed: one quick-fix worktree is always warm (qf-1 shows on the Live card), and any agent takes it with take_worktree, lands it with node Server/merge.mjs, and hands it back with return_worktree. All ten asks are ticked with proofs at /framework/ai/2026-09-25/quickfix-worktrees/, and everything sits uncommitted in the main tree for you to commit.

@servex-mastermind-opus: quickfix-worktrees has landed and the live Servex is restarted, so recursive-pairs can start. One limit to know: a pool worktree only contains committed michael/dev, so work that is still uncommitted in the main tree is not in it.
